title: Keep ancilla preparation distinct from full Gibbs mixing
statement: If the same decoded logical channel preserves basis-state overlap fidelity>=1-eta, then sup_omega D(T_t(omega),rho)>=(1-2eta)/2. For eta<1/4 over the storage interval the exact sampler cannot mix ALL initial states to rho within trace distance1/4 during that interval.

requires: For EACH actual H separately: exactly stationary Gaussian CKG dynamics adapted to THAT H, all3n seeds and actual coherent correction, optional same-H drift
One shared exact logical decoder; for EACH H prepare the corresponding Gibbs-derived ancilla tau_H and actual positive encoder
provides: The reviewed full-Gibbs-mixing obstruction at the same logical lifetime
assumptions: Not a lower bound for arbitrary state-preparation algorithms
Not a lower bound on preparing tau=Tr_logical(U rho U*) or mixing inside one logical sector
Neither grant nor rule out efficient ancilla/sector initialization; constructive preparation is separately open
costs: Conservative fixed temperature/perturbation/geometric/LR constants, support-radius scaling,3n per-site clock and onset all paid
Source n_k<=5g^(2k), alpha=ln2/(6ln g)>0; lifetime exp(c n_k^alpha) with possibly terrible native constants
Physical Gibbs-ancilla preparation, implementation of exact filters/coherent correction, controls/readout and accumulated actual imperfections remain unacquired
contract.units: Trace distance D=half trace norm, worst-start full-system mixing; not logical-sector or ancilla preparation complexity.
contract.obstruction: Logical information can remain long lived while nonlogical syndrome or ancilla equilibration is fast.

evidence.quote: # Long memory does not give rapid full-Gibbs initialization
evidence.range_scope: Actual received statement/review at this exact source version. No new scientific audit or program replay.

body: For EACH allowed actual perturbed H, choose ITS OWN exactly stationary Gaussian generator with coherent correction and ITS OWN Gibbs-derived encoding ancilla. The logical decoder is shared. Neither controller nor initializer is fixed before unknown H is chosen. This is not a native physical bath/device, generic nonstationary noise, two-body endpoint lifetime, efficient preparation or useful numerical advantage. Slow FULL Gibbs mixing does not rule out efficient ancilla/sector initialization. Read the exact supporting statement and its applicable conditions. Producer review status is preserved; no new scientific audit or producer-code execution was performed for this insertion.

review.scope: Completed internal scientific reviews are accepted only at their received source versions and scopes. This intake maps statements and evidence; it performs no new scientific review, code replay, physical experiment or novelty clearance.
